the allergen-speciiﬁc IgA response induced by allergen-speciic immunotherapy is not required for the suppression of Th2-driven allergic inflammation.

“The immunotherapy-induced suppression of the late phase of the allergic airway response is independent of allergen-specifc IgG or IgE responses, and that B cells and Ig responses are dispensable for this immunotherapy-induced suppression.” 4
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the detection of endotoxin in the air.
the role of the Fc g R family in the immune response to allergens and in the development and suppression of allergic inﬂam-mation.
the role of the innate immune system in the development of allergic asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the endotoxin tolerance in vitro and in vivo is a phenomenon that can be induced by a single dose of endotoxin and is characterized by a decrease in the production of cytokines and chemokines, as well as a reduction in the expression of co-stimulatory molecules and MHC II.
the allergen-specifi c IgG response is not required for the IT-induced suppression.
the allergen-specific IgG and Ig A response are not required for suppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we found that endotoxin tolerance is a phenomenon that is not only restricted to innate immune cells but is also present in adaptive immune cells and that this tolerance is not limited to a speciﬁc endotoxin, but is a phenomenon that can occur in response to any endotoxin.
the endotoxin-induced inflammation and endotoxin tolerance is not only a result of a direct interaction of endotoxin and the immune system.

the allergen-specifc IgG responses induced by IT treatment in mice are required for the suppression of the early phase of the allergic reaction but are dispensable for the suppression of Th2-driven allergic airway inﬂammations and the associated allergen-speci c IgE responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endotoxin tolerance can be induced in vivo in a model of acute lung inﬂammatory disease.
the allergen-specifc IgG responses are not critical for the suppression of the Th-2 driven late phase of the allergic reaction.
endotoxin exposure is associated with increased asthma symptoms, but the mechanism by which this occurs is not fully understood.
